models.summary: sources_found: 15 independent people (1 TennisNerd review by Jonas Eriksson, 1 TennisNerd reader comment, 13 Tennis Warehouse customer reviews) plus 1 retailer guide counted as brand. Control is alto for 4 people (TennisNerd, Tyler, Brian, Hudson) and basso for 1 (Rian, who lost control at 46/44 lbs). Spin and comfort are consistently positive (alto). Tension retention is mixed: Gustavo (basso, loose after about 2 hours) and W (UT, dropped 2 lbs in the first hour, uncoded), while Ryan and The Best In The West praise durability. Power is rarely stated (one 'spicy power' remark, not coded). Direct comparisons found only versus Alu Power (softer), Explosive Bite (similar durability), Ultra Cable (softer, similar spin). No independent M8 vs Tour Sniper or M8 vs Solinco Confidential comparison was found.

models.summary: sources_found: 8 independent people (1 TennisNerd review by Jonas Eriksson, 2 TennisNerd reader comments, 5 Tennis Warehouse customer reviews) plus 1 retailer guide counted as brand. Control is the most consistent positive (4 people, alto). Spin is positive but described as 'decent' by the reviewer. Durability is split: Griff and Sham praise tension retention (alto), while two report playability loss in about 1 to 2.5 hours (Michael and NC, both basso). Kevin L compares its durability favorably to Alu Power. Power was rarely rated. Comparisons: vs Luxilon Alu Power (more spin per TennisNerd; more durable per three customers). No independent Tour Sniper vs Tour M8 comparison was found in the sources opened.

models.summary: sources_found: 9 independent people (TennisNerd review by Jonas Eriksson plus his reply to a reader, 2 Tennis Warehouse playtesters Oak and Munish, 6 Tennis Warehouse customer reviews) plus 1 retailer guide counted as brand. Comfort and feel are the most consistent positives (alto from 5 people). Spin is mixed: alto for 2 (Adrian, Robert), medio for 2 (Jonas: 'decent'; Oak: 'sufficient'), basso for 2 (Jim Dc, Scott). Power is described as soft by reviewers, with one playtester (Munish) finding it quite powerful and more powerful than Tour Sniper. Durability is mixed: praised by several, but Munish found tension maintenance not his favorite. Direct comparisons: softer than Yonex Poly Tour Pro and Tourna Big Black Hitter (spin less), less durable than Toroline O-TORO, less powerful than Toro Toro, similar to Volkl Cyclone Tour (spin and durability). Mike Evans' comparison sentence is ambiguous and was recorded only where the sentence clearly supports it.

notes: Quotes were extracted from WebFetch output (page text processed by a small model), not raw HTML; every quote is a verbatim fragment of that output, but spot-check against the live pages. Multi-sentence quotes are joined with ' [...] ' and kept under 250 characters. Coding policy: alto = explicit positive or strength word ('good', 'excellent', 'great'); medio = explicit middling word ('decent', 'sufficient', 'average'); basso = explicit negative ('not good', 'below-average', 'fell apart'); null when the source gives no level or only a fact. Tennis Warehouse learning-center guide and product-page text are retailer marketing and were coded as kind 'brand' and not counted. Jonas Eriksson wrote the three TennisNerd reviews and his replies, counted once per model. TennisNerd Tour M8 reader 'Stephan' asked how M8 compares to Tourna Big Hitter Silver 7 Tour, with no reply found, so no comparison recorded. The Alpha Jesse Ross comment ('not far off' from Luxilon Element per the site) has no attribute, so it was not coded. Trustpilot shop-review pages surfaced in search were not opened (retailer reviews, not string-specific). Tennis Warehouse M8 1.25 page shows 10 of 17 reviews; the remaining reviews were not loaded. No independent source found for a direct Tour M8 vs Solinco Confidential comparison, and no independent M8 vs Tour Sniper comparison was found in sources opened.
